job.style: a diary entry or letter by a student

passage: Dear Diary, today my science teacher explained why we must be careful about what we eat. I used to think that because vegetable oil comes from plants, fried snacks were healthy, but she explained that deep-frying destroys nutrients and adds unhealthy fats. I also learned that sugar hides in many places. Even if a snack tastes spicy or sour, it often contains high amounts of added sugar. My friend Rohan thinks he is safe because he never adds sugar to his tea, but he forgets that the packaged biscuits and cold drinks he consumes are loaded with sugar. The teacher also warned us about fruit juice. While whole fruits provide essential fibre, juice is just a concentrated sugar solution that lacks the fibre of the original fruit. Finally, she clarified that diabetes is a metabolic condition caused by lifestyle and diet, not a contagious disease that spreads like a cold. It is shocking to realize how much we misunderstand about our daily food choices. I have decided to stop drinking sugary sodas and start eating whole fruits instead. It is time to take my health seriously before I develop long-term problems like obesity or heart issues.

items.evidence: I used to think that because vegetable oil comes from plants, fried snacks were healthy, but she explained that deep-frying destroys nutrients and adds unhealthy fats.
items.q: Samosas are deep-fried in vegetable oil, which comes from plants. How does the frying affect them?
options: It ruins nutrients and adds harmful fats
It keeps them healthy, since the oil is plant-based
It adds fats but keeps every nutrient safe
It removes the salt and sugar from them
items.explain: Deep-frying destroys nutrients and adds unhealthy fats, even when the oil comes from plants.

wrong.why: thinks plant oil makes fried food healthy
notices only half of the teacher's point
mixes in other ideas from the passage

items.evidence: Even if a snack tastes spicy or sour, it often contains high amounts of added sugar.
items.q: Priya buys spicy chips because she thinks they have no sugar. What is her mistake?
options: Spicy snacks often hide a lot of added sugar
Spicy snacks have sugar only if they taste sweet
Spicy snacks have sugar only when eaten with tea
Spicy snacks have sugar only after deep-frying
items.explain: Even snacks that taste spicy or sour often contain high amounts of added sugar.

wrong.why: thinks only sweet-tasting foods have sugar
thinks sugar only counts in tea
links sugar to frying, a nearby idea

items.evidence: My friend Rohan thinks he is safe because he never adds sugar to his tea, but he forgets that the packaged biscuits and cold drinks he consumes are loaded with sugar.
items.q: Rohan says he eats little sugar because he never sweetens his tea. Is he right?
options: He is wrong; his biscuits and cold drinks are sugary
He is right; cold drinks are mostly flavoured water
He is right; sugar limits only apply to tea
He is wrong; plain tea itself is full of sugar
items.explain: Rohan skips sugar in tea, but his packaged biscuits and cold drinks are loaded with sugar.

wrong.why: thinks cold drinks have little sugar
thinks sugar only matters in tea
blames the tea named in the sentence

items.evidence: While whole fruits provide essential fibre, juice is just a concentrated sugar solution that lacks the fibre of the original fruit.
items.q: How is a glass of orange juice different from eating a whole orange?
options: The juice has plenty of sugar but no fibre
The juice is just as healthy as the fruit
The juice has plenty of fibre but less sugar
The juice gives energy that can replace a meal
items.explain: Juice is concentrated sugar without the fibre that whole fruits give.

wrong.why: reverses which one has the fibre
thinks sugary drinks can replace food
